papers.title: Protocol for correlating in vivo calcium imaging with spatial transcriptomics in the mouse brain.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in neuroscience research is to elucidate how distinct neuronal types coordinate to produce complex behaviors, which requires linking the molecular identity of neuronal types with their connectivity and activity in behaving animals. Here, we present a protocol for integrating spatial gene-expression profiling with in vivo calcium imaging in the mouse brain. We describe detailed procedures for tissue recovery after in vivo imaging, multiplexed gene-expression detection, and the computational steps to register these two datasets. For complete details on the use and execution o
papers.summary: This protocol describes a method for combining in vivo calcium imaging with spatial transcriptomics in the mouse brain, allowing researchers to link neuronal activity during behavior with the molecular identity of those same neurons. It covers tissue recovery after imaging, multiplexed gene-expression detection, and computational registration of the two datasets. The approach enables correlating functional activity with spatial gene expression at the single-cell level.

papers.title: Natural Asp-tRNA Synthetase Fragment Targets Myofibroblasts to Abrogate Tissue Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Fibrosis remains a major global health challenge with limited therapies that only slow disease progression. While the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase (aaRS) family is known to utilize evolutionarily appended domains as extracellular signaling molecules, their role in regulating the homeostasis of the fibrotic process is poorly defined. We identify a natural proteolytic fragment of aspartyl-tRNA synthetase (DARS), termed DARS-N1, that selectively triggers apoptosis in myofibroblasts by targeting latent-transforming growth factor beta binding protein 1 (LTBP-1) on the extracellular matrix (ECM). This
papers.summary: Researchers identified a natural proteolytic fragment of aspartyl-tRNA synthetase (DARS-N1) that selectively induces apoptosis in myofibroblasts by binding to LTBP-1 in the extracellular matrix. This fragment effectively reduces tissue fibrosis, suggesting a novel therapeutic approach for fibrotic diseases that currently lack effective treatments.

papers.title: stFormer integrates spatial ligand signaling into a foundation model for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Recent foundation models for single-cell transcriptomic data generate informative, context-aware gene and cell representations. Spatial transcriptomic (ST) data offer extra positional insights but were not considered by these single-cell models. We introduce stFormer, a transformer model tailored for ST data, which employs the cross-attention module to incorporate spatial ligand genes. To unify different ST technologies with a trade-off between resolution and gene coverage, we propose a biased cross-attention method that enables the model to do learning with single-cell resolution on whole-tra
papers.summary: stFormer is a transformer-based foundation model designed specifically for spatial transcriptomics data, using cross-attention to incorporate spatial ligand signaling information. It introduces a biased cross-attention method to unify different spatial transcriptomics technologies, balancing resolution and gene coverage, and enables learning at single-cell resolution on whole-transcriptome data.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals a T Cell-Mediated Microglial Activation Axis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibition-Related Adverse Events in the Brain.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting CTLA-4 and PD-1 have transformed cancer therapy, yet their immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in various tissues, including the brain, remain poorly defined. ICI perturbs hippocampal-dependent memory function by derailing neuro-immune homeostasis and compromising synaptic integrity. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which ICI alters regional interactions are not well understood. Using bulk RNA-sequencing and MERFISH spatial transcriptomics in a syngeneic murine melanoma model, we show that ICI treatment remodels hippocampal gene
papers.summary: Using bulk RNA-seq and MERFISH spatial transcriptomics in a mouse melanoma model, this study maps how immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy disrupts hippocampal neuro-immune homeostasis. The authors identify a T cell-mediated microglial activation axis underlying ICI-related adverse events in the brain, linking peripheral immunotherapy to cognitive and synaptic impairment.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing Single-Cell Expression through the Lens of Topic Modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP introduces a topic-modeling approach to recover gene-expression programs (GEPs) from single-cell RNA-seq data without forcing each gene into a single program. This better reflects the many-to-many nature of gene regulation, where cells run multiple programs simultaneously and genes participate in several. The method aims to resolve co-regulated gene modules more faithfully than trajectory-based approaches that impose one-program-per-gene assignments.

papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning and computational approaches can model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal pediatric brain cancer driven by histone H3 alterations and epigenetic dysregulation. It highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics are being integrated with computational methods to understand intratumoral heterogeneity and treatment resistance mechanisms.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial mapping reveals reproducible cell type organization and spatially dependent gene expression in gastruloids.
papers.abstract: Gastruloids are stem-cell-based models that recapitulate key aspects of mammalian gastrulation, including the formation of an anterior-posterior axis. However, we do not have detailed spatial information about gene expression and cell type organization, particularly at the level of individual gastruloids. Here, we report a spatially resolved, single-cell molecular catalog of the transcriptomes of 26 individual gastruloids. We found that cell type composition and tissue-scale spatial organization were largely consistent across gastruloids, but meso-scale patterning of specific cell types varied
papers.summary: This study uses spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomics to map gene expression and cell type organization across 26 individual gastruloids, stem-cell-based models of mammalian gastrulation. The authors find that overall cell type composition and tissue-scale spatial organization are highly reproducible across gastruloids, while meso-scale patterning of specific cell types varies. This provides a detailed molecular atlas linking spatial position to gene expression in a gastrulation model.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic analysis of neurons at the glioma infiltration front: A case study.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics reveals localized IGFBP5 expression and TGFβ-related signaling in neurons within glioma-infiltrated tissue.
papers.summary: This case study uses spatial transcriptomics to examine neurons located at the infiltration front of a glioma. The authors identify localized IGFBP5 expression and TGFβ-related signaling activity in these neurons, suggesting that tumor-adjacent neurons undergo specific molecular changes. The findings highlight a potential neuron-glioma interaction that could influence tumor progression.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using S
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify cell adhesion-related gene signatures associated with cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors highlight specific CARGs involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, proposing them as potential therapeutic targets to reduce inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for indexing protein databases that reduces the memory footprint of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, scaling better with alphabet size than prior run-block compression schemes. On RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, it cuts memory use by over a third compared to Kaiju while maintaining comparable running time, enabling efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification.

papers.title: NicheScribe: consistent and generalizable annotation of stromal cells in the murine bone marrow niche.
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPC) depend on interactions with nearby stromal cells to support their homeostatic functions and mount responses to perturbations. The murine bone marrow (BM) niche can be profiled using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), but there is considerable inconsistency in cell type identification, and uncertainty over how populations can be isolated prospectively by flow cytometry. Here, we produced new scRNA-seq reference datasets using purified populations of murine BM stromal cells, which we used to create a bespoke classifier for stromal cells. Our Ni
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: NicheScribe addresses the inconsistency in annotating murine bone marrow stromal cell populations from single-cell RNA-seq by generating new reference datasets from purified stromal cells and building a bespoke classifier. This classifier enables consistent, generalizable identification of stromal cell types in the bone marrow niche, which is critical for understanding hematopoietic stem cell support.

papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: crumblr is a new statistical method for analyzing changes in cell type composition from single-cell data across large cohorts. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs, making the analysis scalable and flexible. This addresses a key challenge in identifying shifts in cell type frequency in health and disease.

papers.title: Mouse lymph node colonization models predict human tumor metastasis in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Aggressive tumor progression and distant metastases of cancers such as cutaneous melanoma are thought to be preceded by regional lymph node (LN) infiltration. Previous mouse studies have selectively enriched for tumor cells with enhanced LN migratory capacity but the mechanistic biology underpinning this proclivity has not been directly linked to human outcomes. Likewise, the exact role LN colonization plays in distant metastasis in humans remains unclear. To translate and conserve findings from mouse models to humans, we used a computational framework termed Translatable Components Regression
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors use a computational framework called Translatable Components Regression to link mouse models of lymph node colonization in melanoma with human tumor metastasis outcomes. They show that gene expression features associated with lymph node colonization in mice can predict metastatic potential in human melanoma patients, helping bridge the gap between mouse model findings and clinical relevance.

papers.title: Variation in enhancer activity across brain regions defines neurological disease risk and shapes cellular pathology.
papers.abstract: Genetic variants associated with neurological traits are enriched in enhancers active in neurons. However, there are many types of neurons with varying functions across the brain, making it difficult to pinpoint insights into disease pathology. We set out to investigate whether cell type and brain region specificity of transcriptional enhancers could reveal new insights into the cellular pathology of neurological traits.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how enhancer activity varies across different brain regions and neuron types, aiming to link this variation to neurological disease risk. The authors propose that region- and cell-type-specific enhancers can help pinpoint the cellular pathology underlying neurological traits.

papers.title: FlowMap: Geometry-Dynamics Consistent Embedding of RNA Velocity for Interpretable Cellular Trajectories.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals how cells vary across states, but these measurements capture only static snapshots of dynamic biological processes. RNA velocity addresses this limitation by estimating how gene expression is changing over time, providing directional information about cell state transitions. However, current approaches treat cellular state and dynamics separately, leading to representations that violate fundamental geometric consistency and obscure biological interpretation. Here, we present FlowMap, a framework that jointly models cellular states and their dynamics within a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FlowMap is a computational framework that jointly embeds cellular states and RNA velocity dynamics into a single consistent representation, addressing the common problem of geometric inconsistency in existing velocity methods. By enforcing geometry-dynamics consistency, it produces more interpretable cellular trajectories for studying dynamic biological processes from single-cell snapshots. The method is presented as a preprint and targets improved biological interpretation of cell state transitions.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Identifies Muscle Inflammation Susceptibility as a Distinct Periarticular Skeletal Muscle Phenotype in End-Stage Knee Osteoarthritis.
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major contributor to disability and incomplete functional recovery in patients with end-stage knee osteoarthritis (KOA), yet the spatial components of disease-associated molecular remodeling remain poorly understood. Here, we applied spatial transcriptomics to paired skeletal muscle biopsies obtained from the surgical (Sx) and contralateral (Ct) limbs of individuals undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA) to define the cellular architecture of periarticular muscle and determine how muscle inflammation susceptibility (MuIS) shapes local transcriptional programs
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics to compare skeletal muscle biopsies from the surgical and contralateral limbs of patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty for end-stage knee osteoarthritis. The authors identified muscle inflammation susceptibility (MuIS) as a distinct periarticular skeletal muscle phenotype, revealing spatially organized molecular remodeling that may contribute to muscle dysfunction and incomplete functional recovery in these patients.

papers.title: Gravlax: an annotation-independent molecular evidence archive for single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: A cell-by-gene count matrix is the artifact of a single-cell RNA-seq experiment that is most often stored, shared, and reanalyzed. It is the output of a computation whose inputs are the sequenced molecules and a gene annotation, and while the molecules never change, the annotation is revised continually. Once the matrix has been produced, the evidence behind it can no longer be reinterpreted. Recovering that evidence means returning to raw reads or alignments that are large, costly to process, and frequently unavailable. We ask whether a concise representation of the molecules themselves can b
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Gravlax is a new archive format that stores molecular evidence from single-cell RNA-seq experiments independently of any gene annotation, so the data can be reinterpreted as annotations are revised. This addresses the problem that count matrices are annotation-dependent and the underlying evidence is often lost or too costly to reprocess. The tool enables annotation-independent reanalysis of scRNA-seq data.

papers.title: A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis reveals transcript-level regulation in alternative splicing. With the rapid adoption of long-read sequencing in bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, reliable evaluation of DTU methods under real biological conditions becomes essential. Current evaluation frameworks mainly rely on simulated data, which can introduce bias and may not reflect true regulatory mechanisms. A real-data-driven framework is constructed to evaluate DTU methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. The framework includes two key components
papers.summary: This paper introduces a real-data-driven framework for benchmarking differential transcript usage (DTU) detection methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. It addresses the limitation of existing simulation-based evaluations, which may introduce bias and fail to reflect true biological regulatory mechanisms. The framework provides a more realistic assessment of DTU method performance in diverse long-read sequencing contexts.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to the environmental pollutant 1-nitropyrene causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice, with extravillous trophoblasts identified as a key vulnerable cell type. By integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with a machine learning algorithm, the authors pinpoint core regulatory targets underlying trophoblast dysfunction.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain, revealing cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics. It verifies and extends prior single-cell RNA-seq findings by identifying molecular subtypes of circadian neurons and their distinct regulatory programs.

papers.title: CellMAGE: cell-type deconvolution for multi-parent population analysis of gene expression.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA-sequencing remains prohibitively expensive for multiparental population (MPP) studies. Existing deconvolution methods treat bulk RNA-seq as genetically anonymous mixtures, but in MPPs, the proportional contribution of each parental strain to each progeny's transcriptome is already known. CellMAGE (Cell-type deconvolution for Multi-parent Analysis of Gene Expression) weights parental cell-type profiles by each progeny's known genetic composition, requiring no model training and no minimum sample size. Validated in 16 Diversity Outbred mice across 12 prefrontal cortex cell types
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CellMAGE is a new computational method for estimating cell-type proportions from bulk RNA-seq in multiparental populations, leveraging the known genetic contribution of each parental strain rather than treating samples as anonymous mixtures. It requires no model training or minimum sample size and was validated across 12 prefrontal cortex cell types in 16 Diversity Outbred mice.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological covariates from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses by recovering true biological signals from entangled covariates.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family transcription factors and predicts which of their downstream target genes also oscillate, bypassing the need for costly and time-consuming bioluminescence imaging of each target. It leverages existing expression data to reconstruct oscillatory behavior, offering a scalable way to study Notch-driven ultradian cycles in progenitor cells.

papers.title: An in vitro System for Studying Osteochondrogenic Differentiation of Smooth Muscle Cells and Modeling Intimal Vascular Calcification.
papers.abstract: Smooth muscle cells (SMCs) undergo phenotypic transitions during atherosclerosis, including towards a chondromyocyte (CMC) state associated with intimal calcification. Although standard in vitro calcification assays robustly reproduce mineral deposition, it remains unclear how well they recapitulate these disease-associated SMC states. We sought to define the CMC transcriptional phenotype in atherosclerosis and develop an in vitro system that faithfully reproduces it.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors characterize the transcriptional phenotype of chondromyocyte-like smooth muscle cells in atherosclerotic plaques and develop an in vitro system that reproduces this disease-associated state, including intimal calcification. This provides a more faithful model for studying how smooth muscle cells transition toward osteochondrogenic fates during vascular disease.

papers.title: Kintsugi decides, gene by gene, where spatial transcriptomics borrows information.
papers.abstract: Subcellular spatial transcriptomics captures where RNA is in tissue, but a single location holds too few molecules of any one gene to estimate composition alone. Every current method fixes in advance where to borrow - a smoothing scale, a cell outline or a factor model - and the fixed choice shapes what is visible. Kintsugi removes the fixed choice and lets held-out molecules decide, gene by gene, how much to borrow from spatial neighbours and from other genes at the same location. On a lung section measured by both Xenium and Visium HD, the data-chosen allocation placed an epithelial programm
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kintsugi is a new computational method for subcellular spatial transcriptomics that, instead of using a fixed smoothing scale or cell boundary, uses held-out molecules to decide gene by gene how much to borrow information from spatial neighbors versus other genes at the same location. Applied to lung tissue measured by both Xenium and Visium HD, this data-driven allocation recovered an epithelial expression program that fixed-choice methods missed. The approach makes the borrowing strategy itself an inference problem rather than a preset assumption.

papers.title: Spatial Logic and Evolutionary Innovation in Human Placentation.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy unfolds in a unique mosaic tissue context. Embryonic/fetal placental and maternal uterine cells (decidua basalis) coalesce, forming the basal plate where immune tolerance is coordinated and the utero-placental circulation is initiated. The remaining approximately 70% of the maternal-fetal interface is comprised of the chorionic membranes, an epithelial-like layer of placental cells that lies adjacent to but does not coalesce with the overlying decidua capsularis and parietalis. It is unknown how these two regions of the maternal-fetal interface, which are comprised of seemingly
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint examines how the human maternal-fetal interface is organized into two distinct regions: the basal plate, where fetal and maternal cells merge to coordinate immune tolerance and blood flow, and the chorionic membranes, which remain separate from the overlying maternal decidua. The authors investigate the spatial logic underlying this mosaic architecture and its potential role in the evolutionary innovation of human placentation.

papers.title: PhenoMapR: scalable mapping of sample phenotypes to single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies often lack sufficient sample size to compute robust statistical associations between a sample-level phenotype and cell types or spatial locations. In contrast, lower resolution methods such as bulk gene expression profiling have been applied at scale in large, annotated datasets, providing reliable signatures for phenotype associations. We introduce PhenoMapR, a semi-supervised method designed to integrate the phenotypic rigor of large-scale bulk expression studies with the cellular and spatial granularity of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: PhenoMapR is a semi-supervised method that transfers phenotype associations learned from large, well-annotated bulk transcriptomic datasets to single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data, where sample sizes are typically too small for robust statistical mapping. This allows researchers to link sample-level phenotypes to specific cell types and spatial locations with greater statistical power than would be possible using the single-cell or spatial data alone.

papers.title: The misplaced mouse Pax6 interneuron subclass: A cross-species transcriptomic reassignment.
papers.abstract: Subclass cell types are strongly conserved across mammalian brains, making the systemic absence of a caudal ganglionic eminence (CGE) Pax6 interneuron subclass in mouse transcriptional atlases unexpected. Through cross-species transcriptomic analysis, we identify a Pax6 subclass homolog in mouse and uncover primate-specific divergence in the Sncg subclass. Analyses of electrophysiological and spatial datasets reveal limited subclass-specific structure in either modality, emphasizing the superior resolving power of transcriptomics for subclass distinctions. Our results highlight the pitfalls of
papers.summary: The authors use cross-species transcriptomic comparisons to show that a Pax6 interneuron subclass thought to be absent in mouse is actually present but was misclassified in existing atlases. They also find primate-specific divergence in the Sncg subclass and show that transcriptomics resolves interneuron subclasses better than electrophysiology or spatial data.

papers.title: Mapping the Tissue Architecture and Endothelial-PEC Network in HAML Using Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML) is a rare variant of perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasms (PEComas). Unlike its more common renal angiomyolipoma (RAML), the unique spatial microenvironment of HAML and its specific progression mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics from three sporadic HAML cases. We mapped functionally heterogeneous PEComas subpopulations and their localized tissue niches. Transcriptomic alignment and spatial colocalization demonstrated a high similarity between endothelial cells and a subset of PEC
papers.summary: This study combines single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics across three sporadic hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML) cases to map the tumor's tissue architecture. The authors identify functionally heterogeneous PEComa subpopulations and their local niches, revealing a close spatial and transcriptomic relationship between endothelial cells and a subset of perivascular epithelioid cells (PECs). This provides the first spatially resolved characterization of the HAML microenvironment, distinguishing it from the more common renal angiomyolipoma.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics As Rasterized Image Tensors (STARIT) characterizes cell states with subcellular molecular heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Imaging-based spatially resolved transcriptomics (imSRT) technologies provide high-throughput molecular-resolution spatial characterization of genes within cells. Conventional analysis methods to identify cell-types and states in imSRT data rely on gene count matrices derived from tallying the number of mRNA molecules detected for each gene per segmented cell, thereby overlooking subcellular heterogeneity that can be useful in defining cell states. To take advantage of the molecular-resolution information in imSRT data and potentially identify cell-states based on subcellular heterogeneity, we
papers.summary: The authors introduce STARIT, a method that treats imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data as rasterized image tensors rather than aggregated gene count matrices, preserving subcellular molecular information. This allows cell states to be characterized using spatial patterns of mRNA molecules within cells, capturing heterogeneity that conventional per-cell counting approaches discard.

papers.title: Inferring gene expression profiles of tumor clones.
papers.abstract: Tumors are heterogeneous mixtures of clonal subpopulations of cells that co-evolve in time and space. Apart from genetic differences, cancer clones may reside in different locations in the tumor tissue and show various transcriptional phenotypes, with specific gene expression profiles and marker genes. Computational tools that simultaneously infer genotypes and transcriptional phenotypes of clones in tumor tissues are lacking.
papers.summary: The authors present a computational method for jointly inferring the genotypes and transcriptional phenotypes of tumor cell clones from bulk or spatial tumor data. This addresses a gap in tools that can simultaneously resolve clonal genetic structure and clone-specific gene expression profiles, including marker genes. The approach enables more detailed characterization of intratumoral heterogeneity by linking clones to their transcriptional states.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing unravels mosquito biology and host-pathogen interactions.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is fundamentally reshaping the research paradigm of mosquito biology and host-pathogen interactions via its high-resolution transcriptomic profiling capability. This review first outlines the technical workflow and data analysis strategies of scRNA-seq, then highlights key applications of scRNA-seq in constructing mosquito cell atlases, deciphering post-blood-meal transcriptional remodeling, sexual dimorphism, and receptor coexpression patterns. Furthermore, the role of scRNA-seq in revealing the cellular tropism of mosquito-borne pathogens, host immune r
papers.summary: This review describes how single-cell RNA sequencing is being applied to study mosquito biology, including building cell atlases, understanding transcriptional changes after blood meals, and examining sexual dimorphism. It also highlights how scRNA-seq reveals which mosquito cells are targeted by pathogens and how immune responses vary across cell types.

papers.title: Multi-omics-driven personalized management of advanced HCC.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) management is challenging due to its complex tumor microenvironment and poor treatment responses. Here, using tumor specimens from a prospective clinical trial of combined transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), we perform exhaustive multi-omics analysis including spatial proteomics and transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and bulk transcriptomics. These analyses reveal that treatment response is associated with enrichment of anti-tumor T cell regions that are regulated by cGAS-STING activation within immune-suppressi
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling—including spatial proteomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and bulk transcriptomics—of tumor samples from a clinical trial combining TACE with immune checkpoint blockade in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors find that treatment response is linked to anti-tumor T cell regions regulated by cGAS-STING activation within immunosuppressive niches. These findings suggest that multi-omics features could guide personalized management of HCC.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to characterize the ovarian cancer microenvironment, revealing that chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets drive poor patient outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight fibroblast heterogeneity as a key determinant of treatment resistance and suggest these CAF subsets as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how tumor cells and their microenvironment interact within intact tissue architecture. It argues that preserving spatial context is essential for understanding epigenetic regulation in tumors, which bulk and single-cell methods often miss.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide-based bleaching method that allows immunohistochemistry on pigmented eye tissues, which normally cannot be analyzed due to melanin interference. Using this method, they created a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye, tracking markers like Rpe65, Rhodopsin, and Dct/Tyrp2, and integrated published single-cell RNA-seq data from developing eyes.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms across three cancer single-cell RNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells. The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score (BDS) to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, finding that normalization choice affects biological interpretation more than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that computational pipeline decisions can substantially alter downstream biological conclusions in cancer scRNA-seq studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This paper investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, examining whether gut microbiota and their metabolites migrate to and influence intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify the specific microbes and molecular mechanisms mediating this cross-kingdom communication between the gut ecosystem and the disc microenvironment.

papers.title: A State-Resolved Single-Cell and Spatial Atlas Reveals IDH-Associated Differences in Malignant and Immune Architecture in Diffuse Glioma.
papers.abstract: Adult-type diffuse gliomas are defined by the isocitrate-dehydrogenase (IDH) axis, yet how this biology constrains malignant cell-state repertoires and their immune-modulatory potential remains unclear. We profiled 69 tumors using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics, and resolved seven recurrent malignant cell states: astrocyte-like progenitor cells (ALPC), hypoxia, cycling G1/S, cycling G2/M, oligo-lineage, neuro-oligo-lineage, and neuro-lineage. The IDH axis strongly biased state occupancy and malignant-immune composi
papers.summary: This study profiled 69 diffuse glioma tumors using single-cell, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomics to map malignant cell states and their immune interactions. The authors identified seven recurrent malignant cell states and found that IDH status strongly shapes both the repertoire of malignant states and the surrounding immune architecture. This provides a state-resolved atlas linking IDH biology to tumor heterogeneity and immune modulation in glioma.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper proposes a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe). Instead of picking one method or averaging all, the classifier learns to weight each method differently for each candidate regulator-target pair, and the authors also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates publicly available fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify lipidomic features associated with a colorectal cancer-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The analysis suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and the lipid species CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. The findings are computational and hypothesis-generating, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study performs integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood from patients with acute pancreatitis to identify gene expression programs distinguishing severe from mild disease. The authors identify NETosis-associated transcriptional programs and a stratified pattern of adaptive immune suppression in severe acute pancreatitis, suggesting potential blood-based biomarkers for early risk stratification.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework designed to handle large-scale scRNA-seq datasets, combining a fast Louvain algorithm for initial clustering with a Transformer-based refinement step. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to very large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Single-cell-informed senescence programs underpin a machine-learning prognostic model robustly validated across melanoma cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) shapes tumor evolution and the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet senescence-informed prognostic models for skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a robust senescence-related prognostic signature by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data with systematic machine-learning screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to define senescence-related programs in skin cutaneous melanoma and uses machine-learning screening to build a prognostic signature. The resulting model is validated across multiple independent melanoma cohorts, suggesting senescence-informed signatures can robustly stratify patient outcomes.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify natural killer (NK) cell-related hub genes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The authors construct and validate a two-gene risk model that may help diagnose or stratify COPD patients based on NK cell signatures. The work highlights a potential role for NK cells in COPD pathogenesis and offers candidate biomarkers for further study.

papers.title: Decoding the spatial logic of immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: from single-cell profiling to spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains difficult to treat because immune resistance is organized not only by malignant cell states but also by the spatial architecture of the tumor microenvironment. Single-cell RNA sequencing has clarified cellular heterogeneity in liver cancer, yet tissue dissociation removes the positional relationships that determine whether immune cells can reach and eliminate tumor nests. Spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, and multiplex imaging technologies now make it possible to map immune exclusion, stromal barriers, vascular gatekeeping, tertiary lymphoid structures, macrop
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell profiling and spatial omics technologies are being combined to understand immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma. It argues that spatial context—such as immune exclusion zones, stromal barriers, and tertiary lymphoid structures—is critical for explaining why immune cells fail to eliminate tumor nests, and that dissociative single-cell methods alone miss this positional information.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies ethyl rosmarinate as a SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: SLC1A6 remains poorly characterized in bladder cancer. This study investigated its expression pattern, clinical relevance, cellular localization, functional implications, and potential pharmacological modulation.
papers.summary: This study characterizes SLC1A6 in bladder cancer, showing its expression pattern, clinical relevance, and cellular localization, and uses structure-based virtual screening to identify ethyl rosmarinate as a potential SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate. The findings suggest SLC1A6 may be a druggable target in bladder cancer.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omic analysis characterizes an IFNγ-responsive-to-myeloid-suppressive immune continuum in immune-active hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immune-active hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is commonly treated as a single inflamed phenotype, although its internal immune heterogeneity remains incompletely defined. We integrated public bulk transcriptomic, single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, phosphoproteomic, and treatment-cohort data to test whether this heterogeneity is better represented by discrete states or a continuous immune axis. In 112 checkpoint-high TCGA-LIHC tumors, an inflamed-minus-myeloid axis showed structured heterogeneity but no robust empirical bimodality: the observed kernel-density curve had one prominent
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics to characterize immune heterogeneity in immune-active hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors find that rather than discrete immune states, these tumors lie along a continuous axis spanning IFNγ-responsive to myeloid-suppressive phenotypes. This continuum better explains the internal immune heterogeneity of immune-active HCC than a binary classification.

papers.title: Spatial organization of HPV-associated immune programs across tissue compartments in oropharyngeal cancer.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) is characterized by a distinct immune microenvironment; however, the biological significance of immune-related transcriptional programs may vary according to their spatial localization. We investigated the spatial organization of HPV-associated transcriptional programs across anatomically distinct tissue compartments in OPC.
papers.summary: This study examines how immune-related gene expression programs in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer are organized across different anatomical regions of the tumor tissue. The authors investigate whether the biological meaning of immune transcriptional signatures depends on where in the tissue they are located, using spatial profiling approaches.

papers.title: AI-guided ethnopharmacology for cardiovascular drug discovery: from biomedical data to experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Botanical drugs represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites, yet their translation into modern cardiovascular therapeutics remains limited by chemical complexity, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and challenges in experimental validation. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of biomedical data resources and advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have created new opportunities to systematically investigate botanical drugs beyond empirical a
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can be combined with ethnopharmacology to accelerate the discovery of cardiovascular drugs from botanical sources. It outlines a workflow that integrates biomedical data resources, AI-driven analysis, and experimental validation to overcome barriers such as chemical complexity and incomplete mechanistic understanding of plant-derived compounds.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Reveals Inflammatory Microenvironment and Glycolysis-Driven Epithelial Proliferation in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
papers.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a prevalent condition and a leading cause of urinary dysfunction in middle-aged and elderly men. The hyperplasia of prostate stromal and epithelial cells enlarges the prostate, compressing the bladder outlet and resulting in obstructive symptoms. However, the crosstalk between the inflammatory microenvironment and metabolic alterations in BPH remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing to characterize benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), revealing that an inflammatory microenvironment is coupled with glycolysis-driven epithelial proliferation. The findings suggest that metabolic reprogramming toward glycolysis in epithelial cells, potentially driven by inflammatory signals, contributes to prostate overgrowth. This provides new insights into the cellular crosstalk underlying BPH pathogenesis.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of porcine tissue microarray detecting subclinical circovirus infection.
papers.abstract: Porcine Circovirus type 2 (PCV2) is a key pathogen in pigs that induces host immunosuppression, leading to severe secondary infections such as porcine circovirus-associated disease (PCVAD), resulting in significant economic losses for the swine industry. More recently, it has emerged as a pathogen that needs to be ruled out in porcine xenotransplantation research due to issues related to latent infection. In this study, we established a methodology for distinguishing cell types and detecting the viral transcripts within porcine tissue microarrays using spatial transcriptomics techniques. Rando
papers.summary: This study applies spatial transcriptomics to porcine tissue microarrays to distinguish cell types and detect viral transcripts from Porcine Circovirus type 2 (PCV2), including subclinical infections. The approach demonstrates a new methodology for identifying latent or subclinical PCV2 infection in pig tissues, which is relevant for both swine disease surveillance and xenotransplantation safety screening.

papers.title: An integrated network toxicology and multi-omics framework prioritizes BRCA1 as a testable candidate in benzo[a]pyrene-associated oral cancer.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposure to benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) is a recognized risk factor for oral cancer, but systematic strategies for prioritizing candidate molecular nodes and generating experimentally testable hypotheses remain limited. Here, we conducted a hypothesis-generating, methodologically oriented exploratory study using an integrated three-tier framework comprising computational target prioritization, multi-omics contextualization, and preliminary phenotypic assessment. Network toxicology identified four genes shared between the predefined BaP-associated and oral cancer-related gene sets: EGFR,
papers.summary: This study presents a three-tier computational framework combining network toxicology, multi-omics contextualization, and preliminary phenotypic assessment to prioritize candidate genes linking benzo[a]pyrene exposure to oral cancer. The analysis identified four shared genes (EGFR, BRCA1, and others) between BaP-associated and oral cancer gene sets, with BRCA1 emerging as a testable candidate. The work is explicitly hypothesis-generating and methodological, aimed at providing a systematic strategy for candidate prioritization rather than definitive mechanistic conclusions.
